name: brainwallet_of_the_first_hint
idea: The final page's own command line, read literally as a brainwallet recipe: 'sha256 <our first hint>' IS 'your last command', i.e. the SHA-256 of the first hint is the key itself, not a passphrase for a blob. This builds every candidate for 'our first hint' (the seed URL, the WARNING/CAN YOU DIG IT icons, the Logic lyric, causality, the page's own decoded strings) and returns their SHA-256 digests, single, salted with a newline, hex-rehashed and double-hashed, as 64-hex private keys.
check: 64-hex private-key scan against the prize address 1GSMG1JC9wtdSwfwApgj2xcmJPAwx7prBe and the halving address; the digests are also tried as passphrases for SALPH.
retro: Stage 2: the SHA-256 hex digest of the one-word answer 'causality' was itself the AES passphrase, so the puzzle already uses 'hash a hint, use the digest raw'.

def run(data):
    import hashlib
    phrases = []
    def add(s):
        if isinstance(s, str):
            t = s.strip()
            if t and len(t) < 400 and t not in phrases:
                phrases.append(t)
    ps = data.get("PAGE_STRINGS")
    if isinstance(ps, dict):
        for v in ps.values():
            if isinstance(v, str):
                add(v)
            elif isinstance(v, (list, tuple)):
                joined = []
                for w in v:
                    add(w)
                    if isinstance(w, str):
                        joined.append(w)
                add(" ".join(joined))
                add("".join(joined))
    seeds = ["our first hint is your last command", "ourfirsthint",
        "our first hint", "thefirsthint", "firsthint", "yourlastcommand",
        "theseedisplanted", "gsmg.io/theseedisplanted",
        "http://gsmg.io/theseedisplanted", "https://gsmg.io/theseedisplanted",
        "canyoudigit", "can you dig it", "warning", "warningcanyoudigit",
        "thewarning", "logic", "thewarningbylogic",
        "theflowerblossomsthroughwhatseemstobeaconcretesurface",
        "causality", "thispassword", "shabefanstoo", "enter",
        "matrixsumlist", "lastwordsbeforearchichoice", "yellowblueprimes",
        "yinyang", "wewontgiveawaythepassword",
        "itsinfrontofyoureyesbutyourenotseeingit",
        "verylaststepisatruegiveaway", "promised", "salphaseion",
        "cosmicduality", "halfandbetterhalf", "dbbi", "faed", "btcseed",
        "GSMGIO5BTCPUZZLECHALLENGE", "1GSMG1JC9wtdSwfwApgj2xcmJPAwx7prBe",
        "thematrixhasyou", "followthewhiterabbit", "whiterabbit",
        "ciaobella", "enterthematrix", "sha256 our first hint is your last command",
        "sha256ourfirsthintisyourlastcommand", "ourfirsthintisyourlastcommand",
        "thispasswordshabefanstoo", "shabefanstoothispassword",
        "thispasswordenter", "entershabefanstoo",
        "theflowerblossomsthroughwhatseemstobeaconcretesurfacecausality"]
    for s in seeds:
        add(s)
    forms = []
    for p in phrases:
        for x in (p, p.lower(), p.lower().replace(" ", ""), p.replace(" ", "")):
            if x and x not in forms:
                forms.append(x)
    out = []
    for x in forms:
        b = x.encode("utf-8")
        d1 = hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
        out.append(d1)
        out.append(hashlib.sha256(b + b"\n").hexdigest())
        out.append(hashlib.sha256(d1.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest())
        out.append(hashlib.sha256(hashlib.sha256(b).digest()).hexdigest())
    res = []
    for s in out:
        if s not in res:
            res.append(s)
    return res[:3000]

name: last_words_before_the_choice
idea: The page names its own key as 'lastwordsbeforearchichoice': the last words spoken before the Architect's choice. This takes the Stage 3.2.1 monologue and cuts the word windows that immediately precede every choice word in it (SELECT, CHOICE, REQUIRED, CIPHERS, SOURCE CODES, KEYNOTE), plus the closing words of the text and of each line, and returns them concatenated as passphrases.
check: OpenSSL AES decrypt of the SALPH blob with the phrase (raw, lowercase, spaceless and their SHA-256 digests) producing a readable plaintext.
retro: Stages 1 and 3.2: a passphrase that is a literal run of words lifted out of the clue text (the Logic lyric line, 'giveitjustonesecond').

name: acrostic_in_front_of_your_eyes
idea: The macro phrase says 'itsinfrontofyoureyesbutyourenotseeingit' and 'verylaststepisatruegiveaway', which licenses an acrostic: the answer is written in the visible text, one letter per unit. This reads initials and finals of the Architect monologue by word, by line and by every n-th word, and the initials of the page's decoded strings and macro phrases.
check: AES decrypt of SALPH with the acrostic string as passphrase; long acrostics are also scanned for 64-hex or mnemonic shapes.
retro: Stage 0: the answer was hidden in plain sight in the image, one bit per pixel, read in a fixed order.

name: matrix_sum_list_over_faed
idea: The page literally names the operation 'matrixsumlist'. D4 applied it once, to the DBBI host placement. This applies the named operation to the streams themselves: lay FAED and DBBI out as a matrix at every width, take the list of row sums and of column sums with a=1..i=9, and render each list as letters mod 26 (both A=0 and A=1), as printable bytes and as a digit string.
check: AES decrypt of SALPH with the rendered string; digit renderings are also scanned as decimal scalars and hex key shapes.
retro: Stage 3/D4: the 14x14 placement row-sum list rendered as letters ('IZLKESKGGIPPEN') is the same operation at one fixed width.

name: yellow_blue_colour_mask
idea: The macro list opens with 'yellowblueprimes': the first image's 25 colour events are a two-valued mask, not just a bit number. This cycles that yellow/blue mask over FAED, DBBI, the Stage 3.2.2 answer and the Architect letters and keeps the characters under yellow, under blue, and under the FEFE cell, in both polarities and reversed.
check: The selected letter runs are tried as SALPH passphrases; long selections are scanned for key shapes.
retro: Stage 0: blue/yellow versus black/white was already the bit classification that produced the seed URL; D3 reuses a positional mask over the 3.2.2 answer.

name: prime_position_pickup
idea: 'yellowblueprimes' and D1's prime-position scaffold say the puzzle indexes by primes. Rather than using primes to find hosts inside DBBI, this reads the characters standing at prime, composite, square, triangular and Fibonacci 1-based positions of FAED, DBBI, the 3.2.2 answer and the Architect letter stream, and returns each pickup and its complement.
check: Each pickup string is tried as a SALPH passphrase; the longer ones are scanned for 64-hex and mnemonic shapes.
retro: D1/Stage 3.2: the DBBI scaffold is defined by prime logical positions, so position-class selection is already the puzzle's idiom.

def run(data):
    import re
    out = []
    def push(s):
        if isinstance(s, str) and len(s) > 3 and s not in out:
            out.append(s)
    N = 4000
    sieve = [True] * (N + 1)
    sieve[0] = False
    sieve[1] = False
    for i in range(2, int(N ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, N + 1, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    fib = set()
    x, y = 1, 2
    while x <= N:
        fib.add(x)
        x, y = y, x + y
    squares = set(i * i for i in range(1, 70))
    tri = set(i * (i + 1) // 2 for i in range(1, 90))
    classes = [("prime", lambda k: sieve[k]),
               ("comp", lambda k: (not sieve[k]) and k > 1),
               ("fib", lambda k: k in fib),
               ("sq", lambda k: k in squares),
               ("tri", lambda k: k in tri)]
    txts = []
    for key in ("FAED", "DBBI", "ANSWER_322"):
        s = data.get(key)
        if isinstance(s, str) and s:
            txts.append(s.lower())
    a = data.get("ARCH_321")
    if isinstance(a, str):
        txts.append("".join(re.findall(r"[a-z]+", a.lower())))
    for t in txts:
        L = min(len(t), N)
        for nm, f in classes:
            sel = "".join(t[k - 1] for k in range(1, L + 1) if f(k))
            push(sel)
            push(sel[::-1])
    return out[:3000]

name: one_for_one_four_for_one
idea: The Architect's line 'One for one, four for one' is an explicit encoding ratio, and FAED's alphabet a-i is base nine, where four symbols (9^4 = 6561) cover one byte with room to spare. This folds FAED and DBBI four symbols to one, at every phase offset, and renders the values as bytes (hex windows), as letters mod 26 and as printable ASCII.
check: The 64-hex windows are scanned as private keys against the prize and halving addresses; the letter renderings are tried as SALPH passphrases.
retro: Stage 3.2.1: the EBCDIC block was a fixed-ratio symbol-to-byte encoding of the same kind; D5 already groups FAED letters in pairs for Bifid.

def run(data):
    import string
    up = string.ascii_uppercase
    out = []
    def push(s):
        if isinstance(s, str) and s and s not in out:
            out.append(s)
    for key in ("FAED", "DBBI"):
        s = data.get(key)
        if not isinstance(s, str) or not s:
            continue
        v = [ord(c) - 97 for c in s.lower() if "a" <= c <= "i"]
        if len(v) < 8:
            continue
        for off in range(4):
            groups = [v[i:i + 4] for i in range(off, len(v) - 3, 4)]
            nums = [((g[0] * 9 + g[1]) * 9 + g[2]) * 9 + g[3] for g in groups]
            push("".join(up[n % 26] for n in nums))
            push("".join(chr(32 + (n % 95)) for n in nums))
            push("".join(up[sum(g) % 26] for g in groups))
            by = bytes([n % 256 for n in nums])
            hx = by.hex()
            push(hx)
            for st in range(0, len(by) - 31):
                push(by[st:st + 32].hex())
        for off in range(3):
            groups = [v[i:i + 3] for i in range(off, len(v) - 2, 3)]
            nums = [(g[0] * 9 + g[1]) * 9 + g[2] for g in groups]
            push("".join(up[n % 26] for n in nums))
            push(bytes([n % 256 for n in nums]).hex())
    return out[:3000]

name: yin_yang_self_fold
idea: 'yinyang' and 'half and better half' say the material is two halves that belong together. This folds each stream onto itself: first half against second half, straight and mirrored, combined by sum, difference, maximum and XOR of the base-nine values, and renders the fold as a-i letters, as A-Z mod 26 and as bytes.
check: Folded letter strings are tried as SALPH passphrases; byte renderings are scanned for 64-hex key shapes.
retro: Stage 3.2.2 declared the two halves ('half and better half'); D2 already pairs the image's 24 cells with the 84-token host kinds one to one.

def run(data):
    import string
    up = string.ascii_uppercase
    nine = "abcdefghi"
    out = []
    def push(s):
        if isinstance(s, str) and len(s) > 3 and s not in out:
            out.append(s)
    for key in ("FAED", "DBBI", "ANSWER_322"):
        s = data.get(key)
        if not isinstance(s, str) or not s:
            continue
        low = s.lower()
        if all("a" <= c <= "i" for c in low):
            v = [ord(c) - 97 for c in low]
            base = 9
        else:
            v = [ord(c) - 97 for c in low if "a" <= c <= "z"]
            base = 26
        n = len(v)
        h = n // 2
        A = v[:h]
        B = v[n - h:]
        for tag, second in (("fwd", B), ("rev", B[::-1])):
            combos = [[(x + y) % base for x, y in zip(A, second)],
                      [(x - y) % base for x, y in zip(A, second)],
                      [(y - x) % base for x, y in zip(A, second)],
                      [max(x, y) for x, y in zip(A, second)],
                      [min(x, y) for x, y in zip(A, second)],
                      [(x ^ y) % base for x, y in zip(A, second)]]
            for c in combos:
                if not c:
                    continue
                if base == 9:
                    push("".join(nine[x % 9] for x in c))
                push("".join(up[x % 26] for x in c))
                push(bytes([(x * 7 + 3) % 256 for x in c]).hex()[:64])
                push("".join(str(x) for x in c))
    return out[:3000]

name: faed_as_skip_into_the_monologue
idea: FAED is 570 symbols over a-i, six times DBBI plus 24: read as step sizes of one to nine rather than as ciphertext, it is a walk. This uses each FAED value as a skip into the Architect monologue, into the 3.2.2 answer and into the macro phrase, both as cumulative steps and as absolute cumulative indices, picking letters and word initials.
check: The picked letter strings are tried as SALPH passphrases and scanned for key shapes.
retro: Stage 3.2.1: the Beaufort/keyed reading already walks one stream against another; D4 walks host chunks backwards along the spiral.

name: dbbi_checkerboard_keyed_by_the_page
idea: D6 says DBBI's own best escape pair is b,e, and the final page's last word 'shabefanstoo' carries that very pair ('sha be fans too'). This straddling-checkerboard-decodes DBBI itself (a-i as digits 1-9, escapes 2 and 5) on boards keyed by the page's own words, which is the one board family the page hands you.
check: Each decode is tried as a SALPH passphrase; decodes that come out as readable English confirm the board.
retro: Stage 3.2.2: a keyed straddling checkerboard with two escape digits was exactly the cipher that produced the 'half and better half' message.
